headline: Seven top Awami League leaders sentenced to death for July uprising atrocities
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 sentenced the leaders, including Obaidul Quader, for crimes against humanity during the July mass uprising. Half of five convicted leaders' assets will be confiscated to compensate victims.
details: In a verdict on a case of crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising, seven top leaders of Awami League, Jubo League, and Chhatra League, including Obaidul Quader, have been sentenced to death. The sentences were handed down based on 'superior command responsibility'.

The tribunal also ordered the confiscation of half the movable and immovable properties of five convicted leaders from Awami League and Jubo League. These confiscated assets will be distributed among the families of those martyred and injured during the July mass uprising. The tribunal instructed that appropriate compensation be provided to them through the sale of these properties, managed by the July Foundation or another statutory body.

The three-member International Crimes Tribunal-2, led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, announced this verdict yesterday, Tuesday. The other two members of the tribunal are Justice Md Manjurul Bachid and Justice Noor Mohammad Shahriar Kabir.

This verdict follows a previous one on November 17 last year, where International Crimes Tribunal-1 sentenced Sheikh Hasina, then president of the Awami League (now banned), to death for crimes against humanity during the July mass uprising. This latest judgment, ten months later, sentences the party's general secretary, Obaidul Quader.

The other death row convicts include the party's Joint General Secretary A F M Bahauddin Nasim and former State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat. Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, chairman of the now-banned Jubo League, and General Secretary Moinul Hossain Khan, along with Saddam Hossain, president of the now-banned Chhatra League, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Inan, also received death sentences. All seven convicted individuals are currently fugitives, and for Obaidul Quader, Bahauddin Nasim, Mohammad Ali Arafat, Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, and Moinul Hossain Khan, half of their movable and immovable properties have been ordered confiscated.

The Awami League government fell on August 5, 2024, amidst a student-people's uprising. Following this, trials for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising began in the reconstituted International Crimes Tribunal. Yesterday's verdict marks the seventh such judgment in these cases.

Across the two tribunals, 68 accused individuals have been sentenced in seven verdicts so far. Among them, 22 people, including Sheikh Hasina, Obaidul Quader, and former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, have received death sentences. Of these 22, eighteen are fugitives, while four are currently in prison.

The three-member tribunal convened at 11:55 AM yesterday and heard several cases before beginning the verdict announcement for Obaidul Quader and six others at 12:10 PM. Chairman Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury noted the difficulty in reading the extensive case documents and thanked all involved, including the prosecution, witnesses, investigating officers, and journalists, for their efforts.

Justice Nazrul stated that the verdict copy exceeds 550 pages and is entirely in English, with some parts translated to Bangla for easier understanding. He mentioned that the full verdict would have been read aloud if the accused were present. Each defendant in this case faced four charges, with Obaidul Quader found guilty on all four.

Three of Obaidul Quader's four charges resulted in a death sentence, while one (charge number two) led to a life sentence. The first charge detailed a phone conversation on July 11, 2024, at 5:50 PM, where Quader directly instructed Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain to suppress the movement, asking, 'Why don't you hit them, why do you give them indulgence?'

On July 15, Obaidul Quader publicly stated at a press conference at the Awami League president's party office in Dhanmondi that 'Chhatra League will respond to self-proclaimed Razakars,' thereby inciting Chhatra League against the student-people's movement. Following Quader's directives, on July 16, Awami League activists shot and killed Mohammad Wasim, Faisal Ahmed Shanto, and Md Faruk in the Muradpur area of Chandgaon police station in Chattogram. On the same day, six other innocent, unarmed protesters, including Abu Saeed, a student of Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur, were killed nationwide, leading to his death sentence for this charge.

The second charge against Obaidul Quader states that on July 17, 2024, he instructed party workers at the Tejgaon party office in Dhaka to prepare and build resistance in their respective areas. The following day, July 18, he labeled the movement as anti-government and conspiratorial during a press conference at the Awami League office in Dhanmondi. On July 19, after a meeting of Awami League and 14-party alliance chiefs at Ganabhaban, Quader remarked regarding the imposition of curfew and army deployment, 'This is definitely a curfew, it will be shoot at sight.'

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh reports 7 more Dengue deaths]] and 1,593 new hospitalizations in 24 hours
headline: Bangladesh reports 7 more Dengue deaths and 1,593 new hospitalizations in 24 hours
summary: The latest figures from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reveal a concerning rise, bringing the total fatalities this year to 164 and cumulative cases to over 55,000.
details: Bangladesh has recorded seven more deaths from Dengue fever, alongside 1,593 new hospitalizations in the 24 hours leading up to Tuesday morning. This alarming data was released by the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the seven deceased, four were women and three were men. The age breakdown shows two deaths in the 36-40 age group, with one death each in the 21-25, 31-35, 51-55, 56-60, and 71-75 age brackets.

Of the newly infected, 1,004 are men and 589 are women, with the 21-25 age group accounting for the highest number of new patients at 253. Dhaka Division (excluding city corporations) reported the highest new admissions with 383 patients, followed by Khulna Division with 290.

Since January 1st this year, a total of 55,163 people have been infected with Dengue across the country, comprising 34,311 men (62.5%) and 20,611 women (37.5%). The total death toll for the year now stands at 164, with 86 women (52.4%) and 78 men (47.6%) among the fatalities.

A total of 50,941 patients have been discharged from hospitals this year, including 1,566 in the last 24 hours. Currently, 4,058 Dengue patients are receiving treatment in various hospitals nationwide.

Analyzing monthly statistics, August saw the highest number of infections with 20,536 cases and 43 deaths. Worryingly, the first 15 days of September alone have already recorded 19,317 infections and 67 deaths, indicating a significant escalation.

Division-wise, hospitals outside Dhaka city corporations have admitted the highest number of patients at 9,112. Within city corporations, Dhaka South recorded 6,701 patients and Dhaka North 6,383. Dhaka South City Corporation also leads in fatalities, with 51 deaths reported in its hospitals so far.
